title: Value of Rewards for Paralympic Medallists
what_it_is: Value of Rewards for Paralympic Medallists

sections.label: Paralympic awards and recognition questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about Paralympic medallist award values, recognising Paralympians, raising public awareness, and equal rewards and support for Olympic and Paralympic athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the current value of awards for Paralympic medallists under the Singapore National Paralympic Council Athletes' Achievement Awards scheme; (b) whether more can be done to recognise the efforts of our Paralympians; and (c) whether more can be done to raise public awareness of the inspiring stories of our athletes who go through much more challenges than able-bodied athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether the current rewards for national sports athletes are sufficient; and (b) whether the Government will consider offering equal rewards to Olympic and Paralympic Gold medallists.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) whether Singapore's Paralympians should be equally rewarded and recognised as our 	Page: 21 Olympians for their sporting excellence; and (b) whether disabled athletes should be accorded the same level of infrastructural, funding and training support from the Government as able-bodied athletes.

sections.label: Calls to improve athlete rewards
sections.summary: Public calls asked for improved rewards for Yip Pin Xiu and Theresa Goh, and SNOC and SNPC were encouraged to review schemes with sponsors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: There have been calls by members of the public to improve the rewards given to our athletes who have medalled, specifically Yip Pin Xiu for two Gold medals and Theresa Goh for one Bronze in the recent Rio 2016 Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: I encourage SNOC and SNPC to review the schemes with their sponsors and for more corporations to step forward to support SNOC and SNPC on the awards.

sections.label: Career opportunities for athletes
sections.summary: Athletes would welcome career opportunities accommodating sporting commitments and providing security and dignity on retirement, instead of only a one-off cash prize.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Instead of just a one-off cash prize, athletes would also welcome good career opportunities that can accommodate their sporting commitments 	Page: 22 and provide greater security and dignity when they retire from their sporting career.

sections.label: High Performance Sports system support
sections.summary: The High Performance Sports system supports 1,653 carded athletes across 45 sports at a cost of $60 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our High Performance Sports system currently supports 1,653 carded athletes across 45 sports at the cost of $60 million annually.

sections.label: spexScholarship payments and customised support
sections.summary: Monthly spexScholarship payments are the same for able-bodied athletes and para-athletes, and support is customised to sport and individual needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The amounts of monthly payments under the spexScholarship scheme for able-bodied athletes and para-athletes are the same.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Third, the support provided to Team Singapore athletes is customised according to the requirements of the sport and the differing needs of the individual athlete.

sections.label: Rio 2016 Paralympian funding
sections.summary: In preparation for Rio 2016, more funding was provided for Paralympians than their Olympic counterparts in some cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In preparation for Rio 2016, we provided more funding for our Paralympians than their Olympic counterparts in some cases.

sections.label: Monetary awards for athletes
sections.summary: Yip Pin Xiu will receive $400,000 for two medals at $200,000 each, while Joseph Schooling receives $1 million under a $1 million cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Indeed, Yip Pin Xiu will be getting $400,000 in terms of monetary award.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: SNPC has stated before the Games, that there will be an award of $200,000 per medal and, because Pin Xiu has gotten two medals, so, it will be $400,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: They have a $1 million cap, regardless of the number of gold medals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, Joseph Schooling will be receiving $1 million for his medal.

sections.label: Government support for athletes
sections.summary: The Government says its support system does not discriminate between able-bodied and disabled athletes, with stipends and allowances exactly the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As far as the Government is concerned, our primary focus is to help our athletes who are driven, motivated and courageous to have the same opportunities to step on that podium, and that support system does not discriminate between able-bodied and disabled athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, the stipend, the allowance, they get from us is exactly the same.
